Maya: Heads-up — I recreated a 3x tail-latency regression on L40s during the mixed-seq benchmark after the kernel-selector change.

Maya: Repro steps: run the seq-sweep with mixed seq distribution (short-heavy + a few long tails) and batch sweep.

Maya: Command I used:
```
./run_attn_bench --gpu l40s --model vicuna-13b --seq-dist "short:0.85,mid:0.1,long:0.05" --seqs 32,128,512 --bs 1,8,32 --kernels flash,paged,fused --runs 30
```

Kai: ugh. Which kernel did selector pick?

Maya: By default it picked `flash_variant_v2` for short/med but fell back to `paged_fused_v1` for long tails — that's where wallclock latency jumps.

perf-bot: New perf artifact uploaded — flamegraph + nvprof trace: https://artifacts.redwood/perf/1719509000/l40s-mixseq-flame.html :zap:

Sophia: I skimmed the flamegraph. There's a huge memcpy spike right before the fused paged kernel. Looks like KV cache spill path triggers an extra device->host roundtrip for a subset of requests.

Alex: Can you paste the short summary numbers? P95/P99 etc.

Maya: Summary (median of 30 runs):
- mixed short-heavy sweep (bs=8): median latency 18ms -> unchanged
- long-tail runs (bs=8, seq=512): p95 220ms -> previously 75ms
- p99 480ms -> previously 160ms

Maya: Key observation: when the sequence mix includes >3% long sequences, the selector flips to `paged_fused_v1` for the batch and triggers a KV eviction path that wasn't exercised in pure-long or pure-short runs.

Kai: That explains why CI pure-seq sweeps missed it. Our selector heuristic uses max_seq_in_batch to choose kernel — it doesn't account for percent-long.

Sophia: Proposed short fix: add a heuristic threshold 'long_seq_fraction' so we avoid fused-paged for batches with few long sequences and prefer a hybrid fallback that keeps flash for short tokens and switched kernel for long only.

Alex: Another datapoint: I ran a microbench where I forced kernel to `flash_streaming` for mixed batches — latency improves but token throughput drops ~8% for long sequences. Tradeoff worth exploring.

Maya: From nvprof: memcopy (cudaMemcpyAsync) accounts for ~35% of extra tail latency in fallback path. Also saw kernel launch serialization when splice path engages.

Kai: Action items:
1) Add `long_seq_fraction` parameter to selector and try 0.1 as initial cutoff (Kai)
2) Instrument KV cache spill path to avoid host roundtrip on L40s if possible (Sophia)
3) Add a perf test that uses mixed-seq distributions to CI (Maya)
4) Roll back selector change on canary if we don't have a mitigation by EOD (Alex)

Maya: I'll post diffs for the perf CI job and link run history. Also keeping the raw traces in artifacts.

perf-bot: CI perf job draft created: https://ci.redwood/jobs/attn-mixseq-l40s (pending review)

Sophia: I'll look into KV spill path — initial hunch: we serialize KV cache eviction to host to consolidate pages; we can try an in-GPU merge instead.

Alex: If someone can reproduce a minimal failing script, I can bisect the kernel selector commit. Maya, can you drop the minimal repro here?

Maya: Minimal repro attached as gist: https://gist.github.com/maya/2d4f8a0 (script uses the `--mix` flag above).

Kai: I'll push a selector patch that considers fraction and test overnight on canary L40s.

Maya: Thanks all — tagging @perf-bot for artifact retention :hourglass_flowing_sand:

perf-bot: Artifacts pinned for 7 days.

Alex: Good. Keep updates in this thread and ping if p99 stays >300ms after fixes.
